decks.module: The GDL program and the early bird road
decks.domain: Graduated licensing, permits, non-driver ID and registries

cards.front: When did New Jersey start its graduated licensing program, what does it do, and what age does it set for an unrestricted license?
cards.back: New Jersey began its Graduated Driver License (GDL) Program in two thousand one; it phases in privileges for first-time drivers, extends practice time and sets eighteen as the minimum age for an unrestricted basic license.

cards.front: How does the early bird road begin, and what three things does the applicant need?
cards.back: GDL Option A, the early bird road, begins with a special learner permit at age sixteen or older, signed parent or guardian consent, and enrollment in an approved behind-the-wheel training course.

cards.front: What must the applicant provide before the instructor can buy the special learner permit?
cards.back: The instructor can purchase the special learner permit once the applicant has filled out the form and supplied six points of ID, proof of home address and proof of Social Security number.

cards.front: Who buys the special learner permit, and how long does it stay valid?
cards.back: The instructor buys the special learner permit, and it stays valid for two years.

cards.front: How long is the special learner permit itself valid once the instructor buys it?
cards.back: The special learner permit itself is valid for two years once the instructor buys it.

cards.front: On the early bird road, who buys the permit, which tests are passed, and when is the permit validated?
cards.back: On Option A an approved instructor buys the permit, the applicant must pass the knowledge and vision tests, and the MVC validates the permit only once the training course is complete.

cards.front: What is the approved course behind a special learner permit, and what time does not count toward it?
cards.back: The approved course behind a special learner permit is six full hours of behind-the-wheel teaching in a car with dual controls, and time spent at the MVC buying the permit or testing does not count.

cards.front: After the training course, where must the special learner permit holder go before practicing?
cards.back: After finishing the training course and before practicing, the special learner permit holder must get the permit validated at a Licensing Center that has a Driver Testing Center.

cards.front: When may a new permit first be used for practice driving?
cards.back: A permit may not be used for practice driving until an MVC Driver Testing Center has validated it.

cards.front: What makes the early bird road different from the other graduated license roads?
cards.back: Option A, the early bird road, is the only road where an approved instructor buys the permit and the MVC validates it only after the behind-the-wheel course.

decks.module: From supervised practice to a basic license
decks.domain: Graduated licensing, permits, non-driver ID and registries

cards.front: How long and how many hours must early bird road supervised practice last, and what must the vehicle show?
cards.back: Option A supervised practice lasts at least six months and must total at least fifty driving hours, ten of them in darkness, with red GDL decals on the vehicle.

cards.front: Which form records a new driver's supervised practice, who completes it, and when is it turned in?
cards.back: A parent, guardian or supervising driver fills out a Certification of Supervised Driving form, and the applicant hands it in at the time of licensing.

cards.front: What three conditions must be met for the early bird road probationary license?
cards.back: The Option A probationary license requires six months of supervised driving without suspensions or postponements, a passed MVC road test, and an age of at least seventeen.

cards.front: After the probationary license on the early bird road, what must happen before the basic license?
cards.back: Option A then requires at least one year of unsupervised driving under probationary restrictions, and the basic license comes at age eighteen or older.

cards.front: What must a driver do when the probationary period ends, and what happens if they skip it?
cards.back: After the standard twelve-month probationary period, the driver must visit a Licensing Center to upgrade to a basic license, or the probationary restrictions keep applying and can be enforced by police.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, permits, non-driver ID and registries

cards.front: How does the young adult road begin, and when is a parent's consent needed?
cards.back: GDL Option B, the young adult road, begins with an examination permit at age seventeen or older after passing the knowledge and vision tests, with parent or guardian consent if under eighteen.

cards.front: Who can get an examination permit, and what does it not require?
cards.back: A New Jersey resident aged seventeen or older who is not suspended can get an examination permit, which needs neither student status nor an instructor.

cards.front: How does a special learner permit differ from an examination permit in who it is tied to?
cards.back: A special learner permit is tied to a student in a training course with an instructor, while an examination permit needs neither student status nor an instructor.

cards.front: What supervised practice does the young adult road require before the road test?
cards.back: Option B also requires at least six months of supervised practice with at least fifty hours, ten of them after dark, followed by a passed road test.

cards.front: How does the young adult road end?
cards.back: Option B ends with the basic license at age eighteen or older after one year of unsupervised driving under probationary restrictions.

cards.front: How does the adult road begin?
cards.back: GDL Option C, the adult road, begins with an examination permit at age twenty-one or older after passing the knowledge and vision tests.

cards.front: What supervised and unsupervised driving does the adult road require?
cards.back: Option C requires at least three months of supervised practice with no suspensions or postponements before the road test, then one year of unsupervised driving before the basic license.

cards.front: What does the adult road chart list for supervised practice, and what does it leave out?
cards.back: Option C, the adult road for ages twenty-one and up, lists only three months of supervised practice on its chart, with no practice-hour minimum.

cards.front: How long do knowledge test and vision screening results stay good?
cards.back: Knowledge test and vision screening results are good for two years.

cards.front: Besides the permit, what else stays valid for two years?
cards.back: Knowledge test and vision screening results also remain valid for two years.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, permits, non-driver ID and registries

cards.front: During which hours may permit and probationary license holders not drive?
cards.back: Special learner permit, examination permit and probationary license holders may not drive between eleven oh one pm and five am.

cards.front: How can a young permit or probationary driver legally drive late at night for a job or worship?
cards.back: A permit or probationary driver under twenty-one may drive during the prohibited hours for work or religious reasons only while carrying a signed certification on the employer's or religious institution's official letterhead.

cards.front: What does the work or religion exemption cover, and what must the driver carry?
cards.back: The work or religion exemption covers only the prohibited driving hours, and the driver must carry the signed letterhead certification while driving then.

cards.front: What do all three graduated license stages forbid while driving?
cards.back: All three GDL stages forbid hand-held and hands-free cell phones and every other electronic device while driving.

cards.front: Who may sit in the front seat as a permit holder's supervising driver?
cards.back: A permit holder must have a front-seat supervising driver who is at least twenty-one, holds a valid New Jersey license and has at least three years of driving experience.

cards.front: If a student driver commits a traffic offense, who is held responsible?
cards.back: If a student driver commits a traffic offense, both the student and the instructor or adult supervising driver are held responsible.

cards.front: What can happen to a driver who ignores the graduated license restrictions?
cards.back: Ignoring GDL restrictions can lead to a one hundred dollars fine or a suspension of the motorist's driving privilege.
cards.memory_hook: break the rules, pay or park

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, permits, non-driver ID and registries

cards.front: Which passengers may a special learner permit holder carry?
cards.back: A special learner permit holder may carry any parent, guardian or dependent plus one additional passenger.

cards.front: Which passengers may examination permit and probationary license holders carry?
cards.back: Examination permit and probationary license holders may carry their dependents plus one other person, unless a parent or guardian is riding along.

cards.front: How do the passenger limits differ between a special learner permit and an examination permit?
cards.back: Passenger limits differ by permit: a special learner permit allows any parent, guardian or dependent plus one more passenger, while an examination permit allows dependents plus one more unless a parent or guardian rides along.

cards.front: What must every person in a graduated license driver's car wear, and where must the decals be?
cards.back: The GDL driver and every passenger must wear seat belts, and the decals must be displayed on the license plates.

cards.front: Where do graduated license drivers under twenty-one place their red reflective decals?
cards.back: GDL drivers under twenty-one put one red reflective decal on the top left corner of the rear license plate and one on the top left corner of the front plate.

cards.front: How do new drivers get their removable decals, and what do extra pairs cost?
cards.back: Two removable decals come with the permit for a four dollars fee, and extra pairs cost four dollars at any MVC Licensing Center.

cards.front: Which restrictions stop applying when an examination permit or probationary holder reaches twenty-one?
cards.back: When an examination permit or probationary license holder is twenty-one or older, the hour, passenger and decal restrictions no longer apply.

cards.front: Which restrictions does the age twenty-one footnote lift, and which rules does it leave unmentioned?
cards.back: For examination permit and probationary license holders aged twenty-one or older, the footnote lifts only the hour, passenger and decal restrictions; it does not mention the phone ban or the seat belt rule.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, permits, non-driver ID and registries

cards.front: Does a motorist with a valid license from another state still need a driver examination permit?
cards.back: A driver examination permit is required even if the motorist already holds a valid license from another state.

cards.front: How long do drivers moving from another state have to buy an examination permit?
cards.back: Drivers arriving from another state must purchase a New Jersey examination permit within sixty days after becoming permanent residents, or when the old license expires if that happens first.

cards.front: Which out-of-state drivers who move to New Jersey come under the graduated license program?
cards.back: Out-of-state drivers under eighteen who move to New Jersey fall under the GDL Program.

cards.front: Which test must out-of-state applicants still pass, and when are the other tests waived?
cards.back: Out-of-state applicants must pass a vision screening, but the knowledge and road tests are waived with a valid non-probationary license or certified driver abstract from any state, the District of Columbia or a US territory.

cards.front: What should visitors with a foreign license carry, and where must non-citizens get it?
cards.back: Visitors with a foreign license should carry an International Driving Permit (IDP) or an acceptable English translation, and non-citizens must get the IDP in their own country before traveling.

cards.front: What can an International Driving Permit do, and what can it never do?
cards.back: An IDP is an official document but can never replace a driver license; it only adds identification and helps across language barriers.

cards.front: Why must a visitor still carry a valid driver license along with an International Driving Permit?
cards.back: An International Driving Permit adds identification and translation, but a valid driver license must still be carried because the permit cannot replace it.

decks.domain: Graduated licensing, permits, non-driver ID and registries

cards.front: Who may apply for a non-driver ID card, and when must it be given up?
cards.back: Anyone aged fourteen or older without a valid driver license may apply for a non-driver ID card, which must be given up when the person receives a New Jersey driver license.

cards.front: What puts the words organ donor on your license?
cards.back: Answering yes to organ donation at an MVC Licensing Center puts the words organ donor on your license.

cards.front: When is a person asked about the Donate Life Registry at the MVC?
cards.back: At age fourteen a non-driver ID applicant is asked about the Donate Life Registry, and the question comes again at eighteen when applying for an unrestricted license or renewing.

cards.front: Who can register as an organ and tissue donor, and what does it cost the family?
cards.back: Anyone fourteen or older can register as an organ and tissue donor; the family pays nothing, funeral arrangements are not affected, and organs are shared through a national list.

cards.front: What does the Next-of-Kin Registry under Sara's Law store, and who uses it?
cards.back: The Next-of-Kin Registry (Sara's Law) lets people aged fourteen or older store emergency contacts with the MVC, used only by police to reach them after a crash leaves the person unable to communicate.

cards.front: Who may use the Next-of-Kin Registry, and how can contacts be registered?
cards.back: The Next-of-Kin Registry is open to holders of any MVC-issued license, permit or non-driver ID, including a boat license, and contacts can be registered online or by a mailed form.

cards.front: Under the National Voter Registration Act, what must motor vehicle offices offer, and to whom?
cards.back: Under the National Voter Registration Act, motor vehicle offices must offer voter registration to anyone applying for or renewing a license or ID, or changing an address.

cards.front: Which drivers get a hearing-impaired license, how is it marked, and who verifies it?
cards.back: A hearing-impaired driver license, for a loss of forty-one decibels or more, is marked with a numerical code and needs verification by a physician or audiologist.

decks.domain: GDL permit confusables, donor and hearing-impaired options, and commercial license classes

cards.front: How many commercial license classes are there, and what must you hold before applying for one?
cards.back: There are three commercial license classes, A, B and C, and none can be applied for without a valid basic Class D New Jersey license or a valid out-of-state CDL.
cards.memory_hook: Class D before A, B, C

cards.front: When is a Class A license needed, and which other classes does it cover?
cards.back: A Class A license is needed for a tractor trailer or other combination rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more when the towed vehicle is rated above ten thousand pounds, and it also covers Classes B, C and D with the proper endorsements.

cards.front: Which vehicles and buses does a Class B license cover?
cards.back: A Class B license covers any vehicle rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, including one towing a trailer rated at ten thousand pounds or less, and buses that size built for sixteen or more passengers counting the driver.

cards.front: Which vehicles does a Class C license cover?
cards.back: A Class C license covers lighter vehicles placarded for hazardous material, buses under twenty-six thousand one pounds built for sixteen or more passengers, and vehicles carrying eight to fifteen passengers for hire.

cards.front: Which drivers do not need a commercial driver license?
cards.back: Taxi drivers, funeral procession drivers, rescue and firefighting apparatus operators, farmers hauling within one hundred fifty miles of their farms, and personal-use RV drivers do not need a CDL.

cards.front: What does the passenger endorsement require, and which endorsements does a school bus driver need?
cards.back: The passenger endorsement P requires a road test, age twenty-one and three years of driving experience, and a school bus driver needs both the S and the P endorsements.

cards.front: What do the hazardous materials and tanker endorsements each require?
cards.back: The hazardous materials endorsement H requires a knowledge test, age twenty-one, and training with retesting every two years, while the tanker endorsement N requires a knowledge test.

cards.front: What does restriction L mean on a commercial license, and where do all CDL tests come from?
cards.back: Restriction L on a commercial license means the driver may not operate a vehicle equipped with air brakes, and all CDL tests come from the separate Commercial Driver Manual.

recaps.module: The GDL program and the early bird road

recap_hooks.text: New Jersey's graduated program eases new drivers in, and the early bird road starts at sixteen with consent and a course.
The instructor buys the special learner permit, good for two years, and no practice happens until it is validated.

recaps.module: From supervised practice to a basic license

recap_hooks.text: Early bird drivers log six months and fifty hours, ten in darkness, then pass the road test for a probationary license at seventeen or older.
A year of probation leads to the basic license, but only an upgrade visit ends the restrictions.
The young adult road opens at seventeen and the adult road at twenty-one, both with an examination permit and no instructor.
Option B keeps the six months and fifty hours, while Option C lists only three months with no hour minimum.
Test results last two years, just like a special learner permit.
No GDL driving from just after eleven at night until five in the morning, unless a signed letterhead covers work or worship.
No phones or devices at any stage, and the supervisor must be at least twenty-one with three years behind the wheel.
Special learner holders may carry family plus one; examination and probationary holders carry dependents plus one unless a parent rides.
Everyone buckles up, red decals sit top left on both plates, and at twenty-one only the hour, passenger and decal limits lift.
Newcomers buy a New Jersey examination permit within sixty days, pass vision, and skip the other tests with a valid non-probationary license.
An International Driving Permit helps with identification and language but never stands in for a license.
From fourteen you can get a non-driver ID, join the donor registry and store emergency contacts under Sara's Law.
License visits come with a voter registration offer, and a hearing-impaired license carries a numerical code.
Classes A, B and C all need a basic Class D or an out-of-state CDL first, and Class A covers the others with endorsements.
P needs a road test and twenty-one, school buses need S and P, H needs retesting, and L means no air brakes.
